S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.

subtypes.With Depressed Mood: Symptoms mainly include low mood, tearfulness, or feelings of hopelessness.
subtypes.With Anxiety: Symptoms mainly include nervousness, worry, jitteriness, or separation anxiety.
subtypes.With Mixed Anxiety and Depressed Mood: A combination of depression and anxiety symptoms appears.
subtypes.With Disturbance of Conduct: Symptoms mainly involve violation of rules, truancy, vandalism, reckless driving, or fighting.
subtypes.With Mixed Disturbance of Emotions and C: Both emotional symptoms (depression, anxiety) and behavioral problems appear together.
subtypes.Unspecified: Maladaptive reactions not classified into the above types (e.g., physical complaints, social withdrawal).

symptom.disease_info: Adjustment Disorder is characterized by emotional or behavioral symptoms that develop in response to an identifiable psychosocial stressor and become clinically significant through disproportionate distress or functional impairment. It typically begins within a short period after the stressor, often improves when the stressor or its consequences resolve, and does not meet criteria for another primary mental disorder. It is distinguished from ordinary stress by the degree of disruption it causes in daily functioning and from conditions such as PTSD or major depressive disorder by its stress-linked, subthreshold, and usually time-limited course.

patient.stressor_event: Major change in living condition (new home, remodeling, deterioration of neighborhood or home)
patient.stressor: Garrett took a cheap room in an older Bridgeport house with the plan of fixing it up himself, but within days he discovered water damage, unreliable heat, and a landlord who expected him to handle repairs informally in exchange for reduced rent. At first he treated it like another DIY challenge, buying supplies after work and asking friends from pickup sports to help, but over the next month the constant disruption began spilling into his job and social routines. His reactions to the housing stress became maladaptive enough that he missed paperwork deadlines, showed up late to a concrete pour after a night of emergency repairs, and had a tense exchange with his foreman. When the foreman warned him that his apprenticeship toward crew lead could be derailed, Garrett agreed to meet with a psychiatric clinician through a local occupational health referral.

S081.manifestation: I came in because ever since I moved into that busted-up room, I’m snapping at people, staying up fixing leaks or heat, then dragging myself late to work and messing up stuff I normally handle.

add_requirements.Symptoms must develop within 3 months of: I was doing pretty normal before I moved into that room, and this all started within the first couple weeks of finding the water damage and heat problems.
add_requirements.Within 6 months of the termination of th: The housing mess hasn’t really ended yet—I’m still in the room and still dealing with the repairs and landlord—so this isn’t something that kept going long after it was over.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: My foreman told me I could lose my shot at moving toward crew lead if I keep slipping, and I’ve already had work paperwork and scheduling problems because of all this.
add_requirements.duration: It’s been going on for about a month, since shortly after I moved into that Bridgeport room.
